events.title: John I becomes pope after the death of Hormisdas
events.description: John I, a native of Siena, succeeded Pope Hormisdas as bishop of Rome. He helped standardise the Western reckoning of Easter, and died in 526 after imprisonment by the Ostrogoth king Theoderic.
events.html: John I, a native of Siena, succeeded Pope Hormisdas as bishop of Rome. He helped standardise the Western reckoning of Easter, and died in 526 after imprisonment by the Ostrogoth king Theoderic.

events.title: The dying Tiberius II crowns Maurice as Byzantine emperor
events.description: Maurice, a successful general whom Tiberius II had chosen as his heir and son-in-law, was crowned emperor by the dying Tiberius. He reigned until 602, the last emperor of the Justinian dynasty.
events.html: Maurice, a successful general whom Tiberius II had chosen as his heir and son-in-law, was crowned emperor by the dying Tiberius. He reigned until 602, the last emperor of the Justinian dynasty.

events.title: Zwentibold of Lotharingia is killed in battle on the Meuse
events.description: Zwentibold, king of Lotharingia since 895, was killed in battle on the Meuse near present-day Susteren by nobles who had risen against him under Reginar Longneck. Lotharingia then passed to his half-brother Louis the Child.

events.title: Paschal II is elected pope in succession to Urban II
events.description: Raniero Raineri di Bleda, a monk of Cluny, was elected pope as Paschal II after the death of Pope Urban II the previous month. His reign of almost twenty years was exceptionally long for a medieval pope.
events.html: Raniero Raineri di Bleda, a monk of Cluny, was elected pope as Paschal II after the death of Pope Urban II the previous month. His reign of almost twenty years was exceptionally long for a medieval pope.

events.title: Tenochtitlan falls to Cortés and his allies
events.description: After a siege of nearly three months, Spanish forces and their Tlaxcalan allies captured Cuauhtémoc and the Aztec capital. Mexico City, capital of New Spain, rose on its ruins.
events.html: After a siege of nearly three months, Spanish forces and their Tlaxcalan allies captured Cuauhtémoc and the Aztec capital. Mexico City, capital of New Spain, rose on its ruins.

events.title: Marlborough and Prince Eugene win the Battle of Blenheim
events.description: The Duke of Marlborough and Prince Eugene of Savoy destroyed a Franco-Bavarian army at Blenheim. The victory saved Vienna and knocked Bavaria out of the War of the Spanish Succession.
events.html: The Duke of Marlborough and Prince Eugene of Savoy destroyed a Franco-Bavarian army at Blenheim. The victory saved Vienna and knocked Bavaria out of the War of the Spanish Succession.

events.title: The Netherlands cedes the Cape Colony to Britain
events.description: Under the Anglo-Dutch Convention of London, the Dutch formally ceded the Cape of Good Hope, which Britain had occupied since 1806. British rule shaped southern Africa for the following century.
events.html: Under the Anglo-Dutch Convention of London, the Dutch formally ceded the Cape of Good Hope, which Britain had occupied since 1806. British rule shaped southern Africa for the following century.

events.title: US forces take Manila from Spain
events.description: American troops occupied Manila after a largely staged battle with the Spanish garrison, unaware that a peace protocol had been signed the day before. The US went on to annex the Philippines.
events.html: American troops occupied Manila after a largely staged battle with the Spanish garrison, unaware that a peace protocol had been signed the day before. The US went on to annex the Philippines.

events.title: East Germany seals the border in Berlin
events.description: Overnight, East German forces closed the crossings and began building barriers that became the Berlin Wall. For 28 years it divided the city, and at least 140 people died trying to cross.
